answer: Tide-Margin Sybil Resistance: each agent must periodically deposit a marble into a shared spiral ledger, timing arrivals to a drifting deadline set by aggregate demand. Early deposits earn priority; late ones incur escalating opportunity cost, since capital parked for timing cannot be redeployed. Attackers must field many agents holding idle balances through every tide cycle, paying continuous foregone yield. Honest agents amortize across real work. Cost scales with sustained attention, not headcount.
